1.title: Hello from Cali!
paragraphs: Hi Emma, my name is Valentina Ríos, but my nickname is Vale. I am your new pen friend from the English club. I am nineteen years old and I am a student at a university in Cali, Colombia.

My family is small. My mother is a nurse and my father is a taxi driver. His name is Jorge and her name is Marta. My brother is Andrés. He is twenty-five and he is married. His wife is from Ecuador. She is very nice.
My best friend is Camila. She is my neighbour, too. Her apartment is next to our apartment. We are in the same class. Our teacher is from Canada!
What about you? Where are you from? What is your job? Are you a student, too? Are you married or single? Write soon!
Your new friend, Vale

questions.q: Where is Valentina from?
questions.explain_es: Ella dice: 'I am a student at a university in Cali, Colombia'.

questions.q: Valentina's nickname is ____.
questions.explain_es: En el primer párrafo: 'my nickname is Vale'.

questions.q: Valentina's father is a nurse.
questions.explain_es: Su madre es enfermera; su padre es taxista ('a taxi driver').

questions.q: Andrés is married.
questions.explain_es: El texto dice: 'He is twenty-five and he is married'.

questions.q: Who is Camila?
questions.explain_es: 'My best friend is Camila. She is my neighbour, too.'

questions.q: Camila is nineteen years old.
questions.explain_es: El texto no dice la edad de Camila.

questions.q: In paragraph 2, 'her name' refers to…
questions.explain_es: 'Her' es posesivo femenino: se refiere a la madre, Marta.

1.title: New Neighbours on the Fifth Floor
paragraphs: Welcome to Torres del Parque! This month we have new neighbours on the fifth floor, in apartment 502. Please say hello when you see them.

Their names are Luis and Sofía Gómez. They are from Pasto, in the south of Colombia. Luis is a chef. His restaurant is on Carrera Seventh. Sofía is an engineer. Her job is at a big company in the city centre. They are married and their son is Tomás. He is six. His nickname is Tomi, and he is a student at the school near the park.
Their dog is Coco. It is small and white, and it is very friendly.
Questions for our new family? Here are their answers: Are you happy here? Yes, we are! Is the building quiet? Yes, it is. What is your favourite place? The park!
Welcome, Gómez family!

questions.explain_es: 'They are from Pasto, in the south of Colombia.'

questions.q: Sofía is a chef.
questions.explain_es: Luis es el chef; Sofía es ingeniera ('Sofía is an engineer').

questions.explain_es: 'He is six.'

questions.explain_es: 'His nickname is Tomi.'

questions.explain_es: El perro es pequeño y blanco: 'It is small and white'.

2.title: A Day in the Life of a Coffee Farmer
paragraphs: Don Ernesto is a coffee farmer in Salento, Quindío. His day starts very early. He always wakes up at four thirty, and he gets up at five. He drinks a cup of black coffee and eats breakfast with his wife: arepas, eggs and cheese.
At six o'clock he goes to the farm. He usually works with two young men from the town. They pick the red coffee cherries by hand. It takes about four hours to fill ten big baskets.
Lunch is at twelve. After lunch, Don Ernesto sleeps for thirty minutes. In the afternoon he dries the coffee beans in the sun.

He finishes work at five and takes a bus to the town square. He talks with his friends there. Dinner is at seven, and he goes to bed at nine. On weekends he doesn't work. He watches football on Sunday afternoons.
What time does he wake up on weekends? Late — at six!

questions.q: What time does Don Ernesto wake up on weekdays?
questions.explain_es: 'He always wakes up at four thirty.'

questions.q: He gets up at five o'clock.
questions.explain_es: '...and he gets up at five.'

questions.q: It takes about four ____ to fill ten big baskets.
questions.explain_es: 'It takes about four hours…' (take + tiempo).

questions.q: What does he do after lunch?
questions.explain_es: 'After lunch, Don Ernesto sleeps for thirty minutes.'

questions.q: His wife works on the farm.
questions.explain_es: El texto dice que desayuna con su esposa, pero no si ella trabaja en la finca.

questions.explain_es: Con horas usamos 'at': 'at seven'.

questions.q: He works on Sundays.
questions.explain_es: 'On weekends he doesn't work.'

questions.q: 'Late' in the last paragraph means…
questions.explain_es: 'Late' = tarde, después de lo normal. Lo contrario es 'early'.

2.title: Questions for a Night Nurse
paragraphs: Paula works at night in a hospital in Barranquilla. Our school magazine asks her about her routine.
What time do you start work? I start at seven in the evening and I finish at seven in the morning.
When do you sleep? I sleep in the day, from nine in the morning to three in the afternoon. My room is very dark and quiet.
What do you eat at night? I usually take lunch from home — rice, chicken and salad. At two in the morning I eat a sandwich with my colleagues.
How do you get to the hospital? I take a bus. It takes forty minutes.
What do you do on your free days? On weekdays I work, but on weekends I see my family. We have dinner together on Saturdays.
Is it difficult? Sometimes, yes. But I love my job. People need nurses every hour of every day.

questions.q: Where does Paula work?
questions.explain_es: 'Paula works at night in a hospital in Barranquilla.'

questions.q: Paula finishes work at seven in the ____.
questions.explain_es: 'I finish at seven in the morning.'

questions.q: Paula sleeps at night.
questions.explain_es: Duerme de día: 'I sleep in the day, from nine in the morning to three in the afternoon'.

questions.q: What does she eat at two in the morning?
questions.explain_es: 'At two in the morning I eat a sandwich with my colleagues.'

questions.q: The bus ride ____ forty minutes.
questions.explain_es: Para duración usamos 'take': 'It takes forty minutes'.

questions.q: Paula has dinner with her family on Saturdays.
questions.explain_es: 'We have dinner together on Saturdays.'

3.title: Shopping at San Andresito
paragraphs: Mateo needs new shoes for his new job. On Saturday he goes to San Andresito with his sister Luisa. The market is very crowded, and there are hundreds of small shops.

In the first shop, Mateo tries on black shoes. 'These shoes are comfortable,' he says, 'but they are expensive. They cost 250,000 pesos.' Luisa points at another pair. 'What about those brown ones? They are cheaper than these.'
Mateo tries on the brown shoes, but they are a small size. 'They are too small. The black ones are better.'
In the next shop, they see the same black shoes for 180,000 pesos. 'This is a bargain!' says Luisa. 'This shop is better than that shop.'
Mateo buys the shoes and a light bag for work. He is very happy. The bag is lighter than his old bag, and it is cheap, too.

questions.explain_es: 'Mateo needs new shoes for his new job.'

questions.q: The market is quiet.
questions.explain_es: 'The market is very crowded' — está lleno de gente.

questions.explain_es: 'They cost 250,000 pesos.'

questions.explain_es: 'They are too small.'

questions.q: The second shop is cheaper.
questions.explain_es: Los mismos zapatos cuestan 180,000 pesos allí, menos que en la primera tienda.

questions.q: The new bag is ____ than his old bag.
questions.explain_es: Comparativo de 'light' (adjetivo corto): 'lighter than'.

questions.q: Luisa buys a dress.
questions.explain_es: El texto no dice que Luisa compre algo.

options: something good at a low price
questions.explain_es: 'Bargain' = ganga: algo bueno a un precio bajo.

3.title: Which Phone Is Better?
paragraphs: I want a new phone, so this week I compare two models: the Nova 5 and the Lumo X. Here is my review.

This phone, the Nova 5, costs 600,000 pesos. It is light and the screen is big. The camera is good, but the battery is not great. That phone, the Lumo X, costs 900,000 pesos. It is heavier than the Nova, but the battery is better — two days with one charge!
Which one is more comfortable? The Nova is thinner, so it is more comfortable in my hand. Which one is more beautiful? I like the colours of the Lumo: blue, green and gold.

Is the Lumo X worth 300,000 pesos more? For me, no. I use my phone for photos and messages, and the Nova is cheaper. My final choice is the Nova 5. It is not perfect, but it is a good phone for a good price.

questions.explain_es: 'This phone, the Nova 5, costs 600,000 pesos.'

questions.q: The Lumo X is lighter than the Nova 5.
questions.explain_es: El Lumo es más pesado: 'It is heavier than the Nova'.

questions.q: The battery of the Lumo X is ____ than the battery of the Nova.
questions.explain_es: 'Good' tiene comparativo irregular: 'better'.

questions.q: Why is the Nova more comfortable?
questions.explain_es: 'The Nova is thinner, so it is more comfortable in my hand.'

questions.q: The writer likes the colours of the Lumo X.
questions.explain_es: 'I like the colours of the Lumo: blue, green and gold.'

questions.explain_es: Adjetivo largo: 'more expensive'.

questions.explain_es: 'Be worth' = valer la pena (por ese precio).

4.title: Come to My Birthday Party!
paragraphs: Hi everyone! This Saturday is my birthday and I want to invite you to my house. The party starts at seven. Are you free? Please reply to me before Thursday.
Daniel: Thank you, Laura! Yes, I'm free. Would you like some help? I can give you a hand with the food.
Laura: Yes, please! Can you help me with the arepas? My mother is busy that day.
Sara: Sorry, Laura, I work on Saturday until eight. Maybe I can come at nine. Is that OK?
Laura: Of course! See you at nine.
Kevin: Happy birthday! Would you like a cake? My aunt makes great cakes. I can order one for you. Chocolate or vanilla?
Laura: Chocolate, please! Thank you, Kevin. That is very kind of you.
Daniel: Can I bring my cousin? She is visiting me this week.
Laura: Sure! Bring her. Help yourself to anything at the party, everybody. We can all meet in the living room and play music together. I can't wait!

questions.explain_es: 'The party starts at seven.'

questions.q: Daniel can't go to the party.
questions.explain_es: Daniel dice: 'Yes, I'm free.'

questions.q: Daniel offers to help Laura with the ____.
questions.explain_es: Laura le pide: 'Can you help me with the arepas?'

questions.q: Why is Sara late?
questions.explain_es: 'I work on Saturday until eight.'

questions.q: What kind of cake does Laura want?
questions.explain_es: 'Chocolate, please!'

4.title: At La Esquina Café
paragraphs: It is Friday evening. Jaime and his girlfriend, Natalia, meet at La Esquina, a small café in Medellín. A waiter comes to their table.
'Good evening. Would you like something to drink?' 'Yes, please,' says Natalia. 'Could I have a lemonade with coconut?' 'And I would like a coffee, please,' says Jaime.
The waiter gives them the menu. 'Are you ready to order?' 'What do you recommend?' Jaime asks him. 'The bandeja paisa is very good, but it is big. Maybe you can share it.'
'Great idea,' says Natalia. 'We can have it together.' Jaime asks for some extra bread. The waiter brings it with a smile.

At the end, Jaime wants to pay, but Natalia stops him. 'No, it's my turn. You paid last time.' Jaime laughs. 'OK, thank you. Next time I'll invite you.' The waiter brings two free cookies. 'Help yourselves!'

5.title: Sunday at Grandma's House
paragraphs: Every Sunday, nearly all of my family visits my grandparents in Chía. Right now it is two o'clock and the house is very noisy.

What is everyone doing at the moment? My grandmother is cooking ajiaco in the kitchen. My aunt Rosa is helping her. My uncle Pedro and my father are watching football on TV. They are shouting at the screen!
Where are the children? A lot of my cousins are playing in the garden. My little cousin Juanita is crying because she wants the ball. My mother is looking after her.
I am an only child, so I love these Sundays. Is my grandfather sleeping? No, he isn't. He is telling an old story, but no one is listening!
Next month my cousin Carolina is getting married. Many people are talking about the wedding today. Not many people know her boyfriend well, but everybody is happy for her.

5.title: Video Call with Mum
paragraphs: Felipe is studying in Spain this year. On Saturday he is making a video call to his family in Colombia.

Felipe: Hi, Mum! What are you doing? Mum: Hi, honey! I'm making lunch. Your dad is fixing the car. Felipe: Is Grandpa there? Mum: Yes, he is. He's living with us at the moment. Your aunt is looking after him on weekdays.

Felipe: And my sisters? Are they studying? Mum: Ha! No, they aren't. Mariana is talking to her boyfriend on the phone, and Lucía is sleeping. Felipe: Typical! What about the dog? Mum: He's sitting next to me. He misses you!

Mum: And you? Are you eating well? Felipe: Yes, Mum. Here a lot of students cook together. Not many people eat in restaurants because they are expensive. All my friends here are from different countries. Nobody is from Colombia.
Mum: Are you coming home in December? Felipe: Yes, I am! Mum: Wonderful! Everybody is waiting for you.

6.title: My Free Time: Salsa!
paragraphs: Hi, I'm Daniela and I'm from Cali, the world capital of salsa. My favourite hobby is dancing. I'm really into salsa caleña — it's very fast!

How often do I dance? I almost always go to classes twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays. On Saturdays I usually go dancing with my friends at a club. I hardly ever stay at home on Saturday nights.
How long do I practise? About two hours each class. I spend a lot of time on my feet, so I'm sometimes tired. But it's a great exercise.
Am I good at it? Well, I'm OK. My teacher, Brayan, is very good — he dances in competitions once a year. I never dance in competitions. I'm too nervous!
In my free time I also read, but not very often. And you? What do you do in your free time?

6.title: Survey: How Do You Spend Your Free Time?
paragraphs: Our English class asked twenty students at Colegio San José about their free time. Here are the results of our survey.
How often do you watch videos online? Almost everybody watches videos every day. They usually spend about two hours on their phones after school.
How often do you play sports? Twelve students play football or basketball twice or three times a week. Four students hardly ever play sports. 'I'm not good at sports,' says Julián.
Do you read for fun? Only five students read books once a week. Nobody reads every day.
How well do you play an instrument? Three students play the guitar. 'I play quite well,' says Mariana. 'I practise every evening.'

What are you into? The favourite hobby is music, then sports, then video games. Two students are into cooking. 'I always cook on Sundays,' says Samuel. Our conclusion: students have a lot of hobbies, but phones take a lot of their free time.

7.title: My Weekend in Cartagena
paragraphs: Last weekend I travelled to Cartagena with my best friend, Laura. We had a great time!
We arrived on Friday night. The flight from Bogotá was short — only one hour and a half. We stayed in a small hotel in Getsemaní. It wasn't expensive, and the people were very friendly.

On Saturday morning we walked around the old city. The streets were beautiful and full of colour. Then we bought fruit from a palenquera — mango and watermelon. After that, we took a boat to the Rosario Islands. The water was blue and warm.
On Sunday, something funny happened. A parrot stole Laura's hat at the beach! We laughed a lot. The museum in the afternoon was a bit boring, but the dinner was delicious.
We came back the day before yesterday. Two days ago I was on the beach, and now I'm at the office. Life is hard!

7.title: The Lost Bag
paragraphs: Yesterday was a strange day for Andrés. He took a bus from Bucaramanga to Bogotá early in the morning. The trip was long — nine hours — and boring.
When the bus arrived at the terminal, Andrés got off and walked to a taxi. Then he stopped. Where was his bag? It wasn't with him! His laptop and his clothes were inside.

He ran back to the bus, but it wasn't there. Andrés was very worried. He went to the bus company office. A woman there called the driver. 'Yes,' she said after a few minutes, 'your bag is on the bus. The driver is coming back.'
Andrés waited for forty minutes. After that, the bus came back and the driver gave him the bag. Andrés said thank you and gave him a small present: a box of bocadillos from Santander.
Last night he told the story to his family. 'Never again,' he said.

questions.q: What was in the bag?
questions.explain_es: 'His laptop and his clothes were inside.'

questions.explain_es: 'Andrés waited for forty minutes.'

8.title: Welcome to La Candelaria
paragraphs: La Candelaria is the old neighbourhood in the centre of Bogotá. It's small, so everything is within walking distance.

There are a lot of museums here. The Botero Museum is on Calle 11, across from a small library. There is a big square, Plaza de Bolívar, between the Cathedral and the Congress. It's very crowded on weekends.

Are there any good places to eat? Yes, there are! There is a famous café on the corner of Calle 10 and Carrera 2. They sell chocolate with cheese. There are a few small restaurants on the next block, too.
How much money do you need? Not a lot. Many museums are free on Sundays. How many days do you need? One or two days is enough.
Tip: the streets are quiet at night, so take a taxi after nine.

8.title: Apartment for Rent in Envigado
paragraphs: Apartment for rent! A nice, sunny apartment in a quiet neighbourhood of Envigado, ten minutes from Medellín by metro.

What is there in the apartment? There are two bedrooms, one bathroom and a small kitchen. There is a balcony with a beautiful view of the mountains. There isn't a garage, but there is a bus stop on the corner.
Is there any furniture? Yes, there is a little furniture: a sofa, a table, four chairs and a bed. There aren't any lamps.

What is near the apartment? There is a supermarket across from the building and a park between the school and the church. There are a few cafés on the same block. Everything is within walking distance.
How much is the rent? 1,500,000 pesos a month. How many people can live here? Three people maximum. No pets, please.
Call Doña Gloria: 300 555 0123.

9.title: Who Is Who at the Wedding?
paragraphs: Sara is at her friend Kelly's wedding in Santa Marta. She doesn't know many people, so Kelly's brother, Iván, helps her.
'Who's the woman wearing the blue dress?' asks Sara. 'That's my aunt Beatriz. She's middle-aged, but she dances like a teenager!'
'And the tall man standing next to her?' 'That's her husband, Óscar. He has a grey beard and a moustache. He's very quiet, but he's really kind.'
'What does Kelly's new husband look like? I can't see him.' 'Juan? He's the good-looking guy talking to the photographer. He's slim, with short curly hair and brown eyes.'
'And who's the little girl with long straight hair?' 'That's my niece, Isabella. She takes after her mother — they have the same big green eyes.'
'What's Isabella like?' 'Oh, she's funny and very clever. Look! She's dancing with Aunt Beatriz now.'

9.title: Missing: Have You Seen Our Grandpa?
paragraphs: Please help! Our grandfather, Don Alberto Pérez, left his house in Manizales this morning at eight and he hasn't come home. He's seventy-eight and he sometimes forgets things.
What does he look like? He's short and well-built. He has short white hair and a white moustache, but no beard. His eyes are dark brown and he wears glasses.
What is he wearing? He's wearing a brown hat, a grey jacket and black trousers. He's probably carrying a small bag with bread.
Where does he usually go? He loves the park next to the cathedral. He often sits on a bench there and feeds the birds. He sometimes talks to the man selling coffee on the corner.
What's he like? He's friendly and polite. He looks like a teacher — and he was a teacher for forty years!
If you see him, please call his granddaughter, Manuela: 310 555 0199. Thank you!

10.title: Packing for Patagonia
paragraphs: Camilo and his sister Ana are going to Argentina on Friday. Camilo sends Ana a message on Wednesday night.
Camilo: Hi! Have you packed your bag yet? Ana: Not yet. I've just come home from work. Have you? Camilo: Yes, I've already packed everything. I finished an hour ago!
Ana: Wow. Have you booked the hotel in El Calafate? Camilo: Yes, I booked it last week. And I've already changed some money. Ana: Great. I haven't bought a warm jacket yet. It's cold there, right?
Camilo: Very cold! Have you ever seen snow? Ana: No, never. It's my first time. What about you? Camilo: I saw snow in Chile in 2019. It was an amazing experience.
Ana: Oh no, my phone has run out of battery. Where's my charger? Camilo: Ha! You've lived in that apartment for three years and you still can't find anything!
Ana: OK, OK. I'm going to pack tonight. See you on Friday!

10.title: My To-Do List Before the Big Day
paragraphs: My wedding is in two weeks! So far I have done a lot of things, but I haven't finished yet. Here is my list.

Done: I have already booked the restaurant in Villa de Leyva. We visited it in March and loved it. I've also bought my dress — I found it in a small shop in Bogotá. And my fiancé, Esteban, has just sent the invitations.

Not done: We haven't chosen the music yet. Esteban wants salsa and I want vallenato! I haven't found shoes yet, either. And we have run out of time for dance classes. We've taken three classes since January, but Esteban still steps on my feet.

11.title: Review: Hostal Las Palmas, Minca
paragraphs: Last month I stayed three nights at Hostal Las Palmas in Minca, a small village in the mountains near Santa Marta. Was it worth it? Yes!
The place is really beautiful. There are hammocks, birds and an extremely green garden. The rooms are quite small, though, and the showers are a bit cold. However, the beds are pretty comfortable.
The food is excellent because the owner, Doña Inés, cooks with fruit and vegetables from her farm. Breakfast is included, so you don't pay extra.

What should you do in Minca? You should visit the waterfalls in the morning, because they are quiet before ten. You can also take a coffee tour. I really recommend the tour with Don Hernán — it's cheap and very interesting.
One problem: the road to Minca is extremely bad, so you shouldn't drive. You can take a moto-taxi from the village. Five stars!

11.title: Ask Lucía: My First Job Interview
paragraphs: Dear Lucía, I'm nineteen and I have my first job interview next week at a big hotel in Bogotá. I'm extremely nervous. What should I do? — Kevin
Dear Kevin, Don't worry! It's a really normal feeling. Here is my advice.
First, you should read about the hotel. It's pretty easy: look at its website. You can learn a bit about its history and its guests.
Second, you should practise your answers with a friend. Interviewers usually ask 'Why do you want this job?', so prepare a good answer.
Third, you shouldn't arrive late. Bogotá traffic is quite bad, so leave home early. However, don't arrive too early, either — ten minutes before is perfect.
Finally, you can wear simple, clean clothes. You don't need a suit, though. Smile, because hotels love friendly people!
I really recommend a good night's sleep before the interview. Good luck! — Lucía

12.title: What Should We Do This Weekend?
paragraphs: Four friends are planning their long weekend in a group chat.
Juliana: Hi guys! Monday is a holiday. Any ideas? Why don't we go to Guatavita? Samuel: Good idea, but I prefer something closer. How about the Usaquén market on Sunday?
Nico: I'm up for anything! Let's do both. We can go to Guatavita on Saturday and Usaquén on Sunday. Mafe: Sounds great, but I don't have a car. Could someone take me?
Juliana: Sure, I can pick you up. Nico, can you lend me your big bag? I want to take food. Nico: Of course. And can I borrow your camera, Samuel?

12.title: Help! My Neighbour Plays Loud Music
paragraphs: Last week a reader, Tatiana from Ibagué, wrote to us: 'My neighbour plays loud music every night until two in the morning. I can't sleep! What should I do?' Here are some suggestions from other readers.
Carlos: Why don't you talk to him? Maybe he doesn't know. It's a good idea to be friendly, not angry.
Mónica: How about writing a short letter? Some people prefer that. You could put it under his door.
Diego: I suggest talking to the building administrator instead. That's the best way to solve it.
Paola: You should buy earplugs! You can borrow mine first and see if they work. I can lend them to you.
Andrés: Let's be honest: maybe you could invite him for a coffee and choose the music together. Who knows? He's probably up for it.
Tatiana answered: 'Thanks, everyone! I talked to him and he was very nice. Now he turns the music off at ten. Problem solved!'

13.title: Movie Night: Do We Agree?
paragraphs: Every Friday, Simón and his roommates, Kelly and Brayan, watch a movie together. Tonight they are talking about it after the film.
'I really liked it,' says Kelly. 'Me too,' says Simón. 'The music was fantastic.' 'So did I — I mean, I liked the music, too,' says Brayan. 'But I didn't like the end.'
'Neither did I,' says Kelly. 'It was too sad.' 'Actually, I disagree,' says Simón. 'I think the end was perfect. Life is sometimes sad.'
'I don't think the main actor was very good,' says Brayan. 'I don't either,' says Kelly. 'He was a bit boring.' 'You're wrong!' Simón laughs. 'He's my favourite actor!'

'OK, OK, everybody has an opinion,' says Kelly. 'Would you mind making popcorn next time, Simón?' 'Of course not. No problem.' 'And would you choose a comedy, please?' asks Brayan. 'Neither of you likes sad movies, right?' says Simón. 'Right!' they say together.

13.title: Should Students Wear Uniforms?
paragraphs: In Colombia, nearly all school students wear uniforms. Our school newspaper asked four students for their opinion.

Valeria, 15: I think uniforms are a good idea. They're cheap and everybody looks the same. I don't want to choose clothes every morning! Mateo, 16: I agree with Valeria. Me too — I hate choosing clothes.

Luciana, 14: Actually, I disagree. I don't think uniforms are comfortable. The skirt is very hot in summer. Juan Pablo, 15: Neither do I! I mean, I don't think they're comfortable either. And our sports uniform is ugly.
Valeria: You're right about the sports uniform. It's terrible! Mateo: So do I — I think it's terrible, too.

What about the teachers? Our director, Mrs. Ramírez, said: 'Of course, everybody has a different opinion. Would you please write your ideas in a letter? We can change the sports uniform next year.' 'No problem!' said the students.

14.title: Colombia: A Country of Records
paragraphs: Colombia is a country of incredible nature. It has two coasts — the Caribbean and the Pacific — and three mountain ranges.

How high is the highest mountain? The Pico Cristóbal Colón is roughly 5,700 metres high. It's in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, only 42 kilometres from the sea. It's one of the highest coastal mountains in the world.
The longest river in Colombia is the Magdalena. How long is it? About 1,500 kilometres. The deepest lake is Lake Tota in Boyacá. It's roughly 60 metres deep.
Colombia also has very different climates. La Guajira has a dry desert, and the Chocó is one of the most humid places on Earth. It rains there almost every day!

What about cities? Bogotá is by far the largest city. Its population is about eight million people — roughly three times bigger than Medellín's. And the country is big: it's roughly twice as big as France. The Amazon rainforest covers about a third of it.

14.title: Quiz Night at the Café
paragraphs: Every Thursday, El Búho Café in Bogotá has a quiz night. This week the topic is 'The World's Biggest and Farthest'.

Question one: 'Which is the longest river in the world, the Nile or the Amazon?' Team 'Los Cóndores' answers 'the Amazon'. 'Good answer!' says the host. 'Some scientists say the Nile, but many say the Amazon. You get a point.'
Question two: 'How deep is the deepest part of the ocean?' Nobody knows. 'It's roughly eleven kilometres deep!' says the host.
Question three: 'Which is bigger: the Sahara Desert or Australia?' Team 'Las Arepas' says Australia. Wrong! The Sahara is by far the largest hot desert. It's bigger than Australia.
Question four: 'Which country has the largest population in South America?' Everyone shouts 'Brazil!' Correct. Its population is roughly four times larger than Colombia's.
At the end, 'Los Cóndores' win with the highest score. Their prize? A big chocolate cake!

16.title: Then and Now: My Grandma's Bogotá
paragraphs: Our class project is about how life changes. I interviewed my grandmother, Doña Cecilia. She is eighty and she grew up in Bogotá.
What was Bogotá like back then? 'It was much smaller and quieter. We didn't have TransMilenio. People used to take the tram. There weren't many cars.'

What is different nowadays? 'Everything! These days the city is enormous and crowded. People have phones in their hands all the time. But some things have improved. Women can study at university now. I didn't go to university — I ended up working in a shop when I was fifteen.'
Do you like your life now? 'Yes, I do. I've decided to learn new things. Last year I learned to use WhatsApp!'
What are your goals? 'I hope to travel to the sea again, and I want to see my granddaughter finish school. I'm looking forward to her graduation.'
That's me. I'm looking forward to it, too!

16.title: Ten Years from Now
paragraphs: Ten years ago, I was a shy teenager in Montería. I used to hate speaking in front of people, and my English was terrible. Nowadays I'm twenty-five and I work in a call centre in Barranquilla. I speak English every day!
How did my life change? After school I decided to take a free English course online. I practised every night. Then I got this job. These days my English has improved a lot, but I want more.

So here are my goals for the next ten years. First, I hope to finish a degree in tourism. I plan to study at night. Second, I want to visit Canada — my best friend lives in Toronto. Third, I'd like to open a small hotel near the beach in Coveñas.
Back then, I never imagined this life. Who knows where I'll end up? But I'm looking forward to the future.
